IdempotencyKey.description:
Idempotency key: repeating a request with the same key does not execute the operation a second time. Without the header the request is executed as is. The key is scoped to the merchant and bound to the request fingerprint — method, path and body bytes; leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, and the key is signed as sent.

- Same key and same request after a success (2xx) — the operation is not executed; the stored first response is returned byte for byte with the `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header. If the first response was larger than 256 KiB, you get `{"state":0,"result":{"ok":true,"idempotent_replay":true,"detail":…}}` instead: the operation was executed exactly once.
- Same key while the first request is still executing — 409 `idempotency.in_progress` (retryable, `retry_after`: 1).
- Same key with a different method, path or body — 409 `idempotency.key_reused`: a different request needs a new key.
- An unsuccessful response (not 2xx) is not stored: a retry with the same key executes the request again. Likewise, a successful batch operation response that contains temporarily failed items is not stored.
- A key longer than 255 characters — 400 `idempotency.bad_key`; key storage unavailable — 503 `idempotency.unavailable` (a retry makes sense).

Stored responses are kept for a limited time (72 hours by default), after which the key is free again.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

WebhookEventId.description: The state id: the same across retries and resends of the same object state, different as soon as the state changes. A copy of the body's event_id, kept for compatibility; not signed — deduplicate on the body's event_id.

WebhookId.description: The delivery id: the same across all retries of one delivery; a resend is a new delivery with a new id. Deduplicate on the body's event_id, not on this.

WebhookSignature.description: hex(HMAC-SHA256(endpoint secret, "<X-Webhook-Timestamp>." + body)). Absent only on a rehearsal sent without a registered endpoint (there is nothing to sign with).

WebhookSignaturePrev.description: The same signature made with the PREVIOUS secret. Present only for 1 d after the secret is rotated (POST /v1/webhooks/rotate-secret) — time to replace the secret on your side without losing verification.

course.description: The price of one unit of from in to, as a decimal string.

amount.description: The amount in currency_from. Together with currency_from and currency_to it adds a modes block to the response: both conversion prices (instant/economy) with the availability of each mode

currency_from.description: Currency code. If set, only its rate is returned. If empty or the body is {} — rates for all currencies

currency_to.description: Quote currency: USDT by default; any pricing asset, including fiat currencies with a direct feed (EUR, RUB, …)

offset.description: Offset from the start of the list; default 0

modes.description: The conversion quota in both modes; no key — no quota was requested, it failed, or the pair is outside both modes.

amount.description: The amount of test money, as a string; capped at 1000000 per call.

idempotency_key.description: The safe-retry key; empty — every call creates a new top-up.

amount.description: The credited amount at the asset's precision.

journal_id.description: The ledger entry of the top-up; a retry with the same idempotency_key returns the same one.

include_refunds.description: true — return refunds together with payouts (the former behavior of the feed without kind). Default false: refunds are separate, kind=refund.

kind.description: payout — regular payouts, refund — refunds; empty — regular payouts (with include_refunds=true — everything together).

offset.description: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

status.description: Filter by payout status (an exact value from the payout status vocabulary: pending, approved, awaiting_cosign, broadcasting, sent, confirmed, failed, cancelled); empty — all.

amount.description: The amount the buyer entered, in the link's price currency; required for open and range, ignored for fixed

currency.description: The settlement currency — the coin the buyer pays with; needed only if the link did not pin pinned_currency

network.description: The settlement network; needed only if the link did not pin pinned_network

order_id.description: The store's order number from the embedded widget (data-oblodai-order-id); carried over to the invoice and the webhook for matching with the order; not an idempotency key

payer_email.description: The buyer's email — a receipt is sent to it automatically after payment

order_id.description: Your order_id of that object: the payment's in payment operations, the payout's in payout operations. Used only when uuid is empty.

uuid.description: Our id (a UUID) of the object the operation acts on: the payment (invoice) in payment operations, the payout or refund in payout operations. Either uuid or order_id is required; when both are passed, uuid is used and order_id is ignored.

payouts.description: An array of up to 100 items; the fields of each are as in POST /v1/payout.

source.description: The origin label, applied to all items without their own source.

error_code.description: The machine code of the rejection; present when ok=false.

http_status.description: The HTTP status a single call would have returned; present when ok=false.

idx.description: The item's number in the request.

message.description: The rejection text; present when ok=false.

order_id.description: The item's order_id, if it was in the request.

result.description: The result of a single call; present when ok=true.

balance.description: Available to withdraw, as a decimal string.

converting.description: How much of this coin is currently in transit through the auto-conversion queue (economy); no key — no queue.

public_id.description: The public part of the key.

secret.description: The key secret; empty in a repeated sandbox response (the secret is hashed).

status.description: An empty string: there is no live on-ramp session for the invoice.

reason.description: The provider's rejection reason, verbatim; empty if there is none.

status.description: Session state.

fiat_amount.description: How much will be charged to the card, in whole fiat units; empty if the provider did not name an amount. An estimate: the provider's rate and fee move.

provider.description: Which on-ramp gave the best quote at the time of opening.

reason.description: The provider's rejection reason, verbatim, when there is one.

status.description: Session state.

url.description: A signed link to the purchase widget. Empty if a purchase is already in progress: then check status.

offset.description: Offset from the start of the list.

has_pages.description: Whether there are records beyond this page.

per_page.description: The size of the page returned.

total.description: Total records matching the filter (across all pages).

currency.description: The unit of fee_amount: USD for accepting payments, the payout currency for payouts.

fee_amount.description: The fixed part of the fee in currency; null — could not be determined.

fee_type.description: exact — a contractual rate; estimated — an estimate based on the network fee.

percent.description: The fee percentage; null — could not be determined.

is_available.description: The method works on this deployment.

currency.description: The unit of the limit amounts; no key — no monetary bounds either.

max_amount.description: The cap for a single payout in USD; "" — no cap (always so for accepting payments).

min_amount.description: The minimum amount in currency: "" — no minimum, null — could not be determined.

accuracy_payment_percent.description: Underpayment/overpayment tolerance, 0–5 %. Overrides the merchant setting.

additional_data.description: The merchant's private data, echoed in webhooks (not visible to the buyer).

amount.description: The price in currency — what you are paid for the order. The payer can be asked for more: the invoice's payer_amount adds the network surcharge (the cost of accepting the deposit on the chosen network, see network_surcharge) and any per-method discount or surcharge; your credit is amount minus the commission.

currency.description: The price currency code: any of the 23 fiat currencies (USD, EUR, RUB, …) or any coin (USDT, BTC, …). JPY and KRW have zero decimal places.

is_refresh.description: Revive an expired invoice by order_id instead of creating a new one.

lifetime_seconds.description: Invoice lifetime in seconds, 300–43200; default 3600. Out-of-range values are clamped to the nearest bound.

network.description: The settlement network (e.g. tron, ethereum). Optional — see the currency and network selection modes.

order_id.description: The merchant reference; the idempotency key. Strongly recommended.

payer_email.description: The payer's email. If set, a receipt is sent to it automatically after payment; it is also the default recipient for POST /v1/payment/send-email.

subtract.description: Deprecated: % network surcharge on the payer (0–100); payer-facing surcharges are configured via discount.

to_currency.description: The settlement currency — the crypto used to pay. Defaults to currency (only if currency is crypto); for a fiat price set it explicitly or omit it together with network.

url_callback.description: A per-invoice webhook. Requires a registered endpoint (POST /v1/webhooks): the delivery is signed with its secret.

url_return.description: The "back to store" link on the payment page.

on_error.description: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — stop processing after the first error.

payments.description: An array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as in POST /v1/payment; order_id is required on each item: results are matched by it and it protects against duplicates.

currency.description: The rule's coin. Empty — the default rule for all coins that have no rule of their own.

discount_percent.description: Percent, from -99 to 99. Plus — a discount to the payer for paying with this coin, minus — a surcharge.

network.description: Network. Empty — any network of this coin.

enabled.description: Whether the merchant is allowed to pass the fee on to the buyer (an operator decision).

fee_fixed_usd.description: The fixed part of the fee per payment, USD as a decimal string.

fee_fixed_usd_cents.description: Deprecated: the same fixed part in whole US cents as a number — read fee_fixed_usd.

fee_individual.description: true — a personal rate; false — the platform default.

payer_pays_percent.description: The share the next invoice will apply; 0 if the operator has disabled fee pass-through.

offset.description: Offset from the start of the list (newest first).

status.description: Filter by payment status (an exact value from the payment status vocabulary: select, created, confirm_check, paid, paid_over, wrong_amount, expired, cancelled); empty — all.

additional_data.description: Your private data, returned in the response and in the webhook.

address.description: The address the customer sends money to. On XRP this is the classic r-address of a SHARED wallet — the payment must carry destination_tag, otherwise the network rejects it.

address_muxed.description: XLM only: the same payment details in one string — a muxed M… address (SEP-23), address and memo together; the QR code encodes it as well. Empty on other networks.

address_qr_code.description: The address QR code as a PNG data: URI — can go straight into . On XRP it encodes the X-address (address + tag in one string).

address_xaddress.description: XRP only: the same payment details in one string in X-address format (XLS-5) — address and tag together; the QR code encodes it as well. Empty on other networks.

amount.description: The amount to pay in the price currency (e.g. USD).

amount_paid.description: How much has already been paid and confirmed, in the payment crypto; always a string (0 if nothing has arrived). Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

amount_remaining.description: How much is still left to pay (due − paid); 0 if enough has been paid. Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

commission.description: Our fee on this payment — the WITHHELD amount, in the payment currency (payer_currency). The invoice rate already includes the amortized fixed fee — it is not charged a second time. EMPTY until anything has been credited on the invoice (and, for a currency-agnostic invoice, until a coin is chosen): an unpaid invoice never shows zero here — "0" would read as "no fee is charged". For a paid invoice with a zero rate, 0 is genuine.

confirmations.description: The current number of confirmations of the incoming payment.

currency.description: The price currency: fiat (USD, EUR, RUB, JPY… — see pricing_currencies) or a coin. It says how much the invoice COSTS, not what it is paid with (that is payer_currency).

destination_tag.description: XRP only: the numeric destination tag the customer MUST specify in the transfer (the "recipient tag/memo" field at the exchange or in the wallet). Empty on other networks.

document_url.description: A signed link to the PDF receipt of this operation — opens without an API key, can be attached to an email or given to the customer. Empty if document generation is not enabled.

exchange_rate.description: The rate locked in by this invoice (how much of the payment currency per 1 unit of the price currency) — payer_amount is calculated from it. Empty until the currency is chosen.

expired_at.description: When the invoice expires (ISO 8601, like all time fields).

fee_percent.description: The fee rate of this invoice in percent — the one locked in at creation (a pricing change does not affect invoices already created). Already includes the amortized fixed fee. Unlike commission, it is known from the first second and is always present.

is_final.description: true — the status is final and will not change again.

is_multi.description: true — this is a currency-agnostic link; the customer has not chosen the currency/network yet.

is_test.description: true — a sandbox (dev store) invoice: the money is not real, do not include it in live reconciliation.

memo.description: XLM (Stellar) only: the numeric memo (ID type) the customer MUST specify in the transfer — the "memo" field at the exchange or in the wallet. Empty on other networks.

merchant_amount.description: How much has been (or will be) credited to you: amount_paid − network_surcharge − commission. The network costs of sweeping the deposit are paid by the payer as a separate line (network_surcharge) — they are NOT deducted from your amount. Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

method_adjustment.description: Your discount or surcharge for the CHOSEN payment method, in the payment currency: how much the payer's amount shifted because of the setting for this coin and network. Positive — the payer pays LESS (discount), negative — more (surcharge). Empty if there is no setting for the method.

method_adjustment_bps.description: The same discount/surcharge in basis points (this way it survives a rate re-quote). The sign is the same as in the discount setting: PLUS — a discount, MINUS — a surcharge.

network_surcharge.description: The payer's network surcharge in the payment currency: the cost of sweeping the deposit on the chosen network (address activation, if the address is new, plus energy/gas with a margin), locked in when the network is chosen. Empty until the network is chosen; 0 if the surcharge is disabled.

network_surcharge_bps.description: The same surcharge in basis points of the amount due (this way it survives a rate re-quote).

order_id.description: Your order number that you passed at creation.

paid_at.description: The moment of actual payment — the crediting of the last confirmed transfer (ISO 8601). null until the payment arrives. Not to be confused with updated_at, which moves on any change to the invoice.

payer_address.description: The address the first confirmed deposit came FROM — on account-based networks (EVM/Tron/Solana/TON); empty on UTXO. ⚠ This is NOT necessarily a refund address: the sender may be an exchange, the change of a UTXO transaction, or the omnibus hot wallet of a crypto on-ramp if the buyer paid by card. Before refunding money here, check payer_address_is_refundable.

payer_address_is_refundable.description: true — payer_address belongs to the payer, and address may be omitted in /v1/payment/refund (we refund to it). false — the refund address is unknown (UTXO/XRP, card payment via an on-ramp, address not recorded): ask the buyer for an address and pass address explicitly, otherwise the request is rejected with refund.no_address.

payer_amount.description: How much must be sent in the payment crypto. Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

payer_currency.description: The currency the customer pays in (e.g. USDT). Empty for a currency-agnostic invoice (is_multi) until the customer picks a coin — it has no settlement currency yet.

payer_email.description: The payer's email, if you provided it.

rate_expires_at.description: Until when the locked payer_amount is valid (ISO 8601; a ~5 min window, after which the payment page re-quotes the invoice). Empty when there will be no more re-quotes: the currency has not been chosen, a deposit has been seen, the invoice has left created or expired — the amount is locked for good.

refund_status.description: How much of the paid amount has been refunded: none, partial or full (cancelled and failed refunds are not counted).

required_confirmations.description: How many confirmations are required for crediting (depends on the amount and the network).

status.description: Status: select (the customer is choosing a currency) | created (awaiting payment) | confirm_check (payment seen, awaiting confirmations; with amount_remaining > 0 — partial, awaiting the remainder) | paid (paid) | paid_over (overpaid) | wrong_amount (underpaid, expired) | expired (expired) | cancelled (cancelled) | under_review (the deposit is held for review, an operator is handling it).

tx_list.description: All confirmed transfers that paid the invoice. Partial payment by several transfers is a regular wrong_amount scenario; the single txid above is only the last one seen.

txid.description: The hash of the incoming transaction (once seen).

url_return.description: The "back to store" link before payment.

url_success.description: Where to redirect after a successful payment.

min_amount.description: Lower bound: an optional "floor" for open, a required minimum for range

pinned_network.description: The settlement network pinned to the link; empty — the buyer chooses the network

amount.description: The transfer amount in the payment currency.

height.description: The height of the block in which the transfer was confirmed.

network.description: The network the transfer arrived on. On EVM it may differ from the invoice's network: a deposit is also credited on another chain with the same address.

additional_data.description: Your private data, returned in the response and in the webhook.

address.description: The address the customer sends money to. On XRP this is the classic r-address of a SHARED wallet — the payment must carry destination_tag, otherwise the network rejects it.

address_muxed.description: XLM only: the same payment details in one string — a muxed M… address (SEP-23), address and memo together; the QR code encodes it as well. Empty on other networks.

address_qr_code.description: The address QR code as a PNG data: URI — can go straight into . On XRP it encodes the X-address (address + tag in one string).

address_xaddress.description: XRP only: the same payment details in one string in X-address format (XLS-5) — address and tag together; the QR code encodes it as well. Empty on other networks.

amount.description: The amount to pay in the price currency (e.g. USD).

amount_paid.description: How much has already been paid and confirmed, in the payment crypto; always a string (0 if nothing has arrived). Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

amount_remaining.description: How much is still left to pay (due − paid); 0 if enough has been paid. Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

commission.description: Our fee on this payment — the WITHHELD amount, in the payment currency (payer_currency). The invoice rate already includes the amortized fixed fee — it is not charged a second time. EMPTY until anything has been credited on the invoice (and, for a currency-agnostic invoice, until a coin is chosen): an unpaid invoice never shows zero here — "0" would read as "no fee is charged". For a paid invoice with a zero rate, 0 is genuine.

confirmations.description: The current number of confirmations of the incoming payment.

currency.description: The price currency: fiat (USD, EUR, RUB, JPY… — see pricing_currencies) or a coin. It says how much the invoice COSTS, not what it is paid with (that is payer_currency).

destination_tag.description: XRP only: the numeric destination tag the customer MUST specify in the transfer (the "recipient tag/memo" field at the exchange or in the wallet). Empty on other networks.

document_url.description: A signed link to the PDF receipt of this operation — opens without an API key, can be attached to an email or given to the customer. Empty if document generation is not enabled.

exchange_rate.description: The rate locked in by this invoice (how much of the payment currency per 1 unit of the price currency) — payer_amount is calculated from it. Empty until the currency is chosen.

expired_at.description: When the invoice expires (ISO 8601, like all time fields).

fee_percent.description: The fee rate of this invoice in percent — the one locked in at creation (a pricing change does not affect invoices already created). Already includes the amortized fixed fee. Unlike commission, it is known from the first second and is always present.

is_final.description: true — the status is final and will not change again.

is_multi.description: true — this is a currency-agnostic link; the customer has not chosen the currency/network yet.

is_test.description: true — a sandbox (dev store) invoice: the money is not real, do not include it in live reconciliation.

memo.description: XLM (Stellar) only: the numeric memo (ID type) the customer MUST specify in the transfer — the "memo" field at the exchange or in the wallet. Empty on other networks.

merchant_amount.description: How much has been (or will be) credited to you: amount_paid − network_surcharge − commission. The network costs of sweeping the deposit are paid by the payer as a separate line (network_surcharge) — they are NOT deducted from your amount. Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

method_adjustment.description: Your discount or surcharge for the CHOSEN payment method, in the payment currency: how much the payer's amount shifted because of the setting for this coin and network. Positive — the payer pays LESS (discount), negative — more (surcharge). Empty if there is no setting for the method.

method_adjustment_bps.description: The same discount/surcharge in basis points (this way it survives a rate re-quote). The sign is the same as in the discount setting: PLUS — a discount, MINUS — a surcharge.

network_surcharge.description: The payer's network surcharge in the payment currency: the cost of sweeping the deposit on the chosen network (address activation, if the address is new, plus energy/gas with a margin), locked in when the network is chosen. Empty until the network is chosen; 0 if the surcharge is disabled.

network_surcharge_bps.description: The same surcharge in basis points of the amount due (this way it survives a rate re-quote).

order_id.description: Your order number that you passed at creation.

paid_at.description: The moment of actual payment — the crediting of the last confirmed transfer (ISO 8601). null until the payment arrives. Not to be confused with updated_at, which moves on any change to the invoice.

payer_address.description: The address the first confirmed deposit came FROM — on account-based networks (EVM/Tron/Solana/TON); empty on UTXO. ⚠ This is NOT necessarily a refund address: the sender may be an exchange, the change of a UTXO transaction, or the omnibus hot wallet of a crypto on-ramp if the buyer paid by card. Before refunding money here, check payer_address_is_refundable.

payer_address_is_refundable.description: true — payer_address belongs to the payer, and address may be omitted in /v1/payment/refund (we refund to it). false — the refund address is unknown (UTXO/XRP, card payment via an on-ramp, address not recorded): ask the buyer for an address and pass address explicitly, otherwise the request is rejected with refund.no_address.

payer_amount.description: How much must be sent in the payment crypto. Empty until the payment currency is chosen (an invoice without a currency).

payer_currency.description: The currency the customer pays in (e.g. USDT). Empty for a currency-agnostic invoice (is_multi) until the customer picks a coin — it has no settlement currency yet.

payer_email.description: The payer's email, if you provided it.

rate_expires_at.description: Until when the locked payer_amount is valid (ISO 8601; a ~5 min window, after which the payment page re-quotes the invoice). Empty when there will be no more re-quotes: the currency has not been chosen, a deposit has been seen, the invoice has left created or expired — the amount is locked for good.

required_confirmations.description: How many confirmations are required for crediting (depends on the amount and the network).

status.description: Status: select (the customer is choosing a currency) | created (awaiting payment) | confirm_check (payment seen, awaiting confirmations; with amount_remaining > 0 — partial, awaiting the remainder) | paid (paid) | paid_over (overpaid) | wrong_amount (underpaid, expired) | expired (expired) | cancelled (cancelled) | under_review (the deposit is held for review, an operator is handling it).

tx_list.description: All confirmed transfers that paid the invoice. Partial payment by several transfers is a regular wrong_amount scenario; the single txid above is only the last one seen.

txid.description: The hash of the incoming transaction (once seen).

url.description: A link to the ready-made payment page.

url_return.description: The "back to store" link before payment.

url_success.description: Where to redirect after a successful payment.

uuid.description: Our payment identifier (use it in info/refund).

PaymentWebhook.description: Sent when a payment moves to paid, paid_over, wrong_amount, expired, cancelled or under_review. A chain reorganization that removes a counted deposit is sent as invoice.reversed (reversal = true, txid empty) with the status after it. The current status — any value from the vocabulary — can be requested again: POST /v1/payment/resend. Match it to the order by order_id/uuid and to the blockchain by txid and network.

additional_data.description: Your data passed when creating the payment, as is.

amount.description: The invoice amount in currency.

event_at.description: When the event happened, UTC with milliseconds (ISO 8601).

event_id.description: The id of the object state this body carries — signed, and the key to deduplicate on: the same for every retry and every resend (/v1/payment/resend) of the same state, different as soon as the state changes (sequence, by contrast, grows on a resend). Always equal to the X-Webhook-Event-Id header, which is not signed — prefer this field. Always sent by current cores; a delivery from an older core may lack it — then deduplicate on type:id:sequence from the body.

is_final.description: true — the status is final, the payment will not change any further.

network.description: The network the money arrived on.

order_id.description: Your order_id for the payment.

payer_address.description: The address the payment came from (empty if unknown). Refunding to it is allowed only when payer_address_is_refundable = true.

payer_address_is_refundable.description: true — payer_address belongs to the payer and is usable as a refund address; false — it is an exchange, card provider or change address, refunding to it is not allowed.

payer_amount.description: How much the payer was supposed to pay, in payer_currency.

payer_currency.description: The currency the payer pays in.

payment_amount.description: How much was actually received (confirmed), in payer_currency.

reversal.description: true — a chain reorganization removed a previously counted deposit (event invoice.reversed); status and payment_amount are the state after it, txid is empty. Absent = false: cores before this version do not send the field; newer cores always send it.

sequence.description: The global event number: within one object a higher number is newer, a lower one is a late delivery and must be discarded. Always 0 on a rehearsal (test: true).

status.description: The payment status — the same literal as in /v1/payment/info and the history filter.

test.description: Present only on a rehearsal (/v1/test-webhook/*, /v1/payment/testing-webhook) and always true — inside the signature. A live event never carries this field: your handler must ignore a body with test: true even if the signature is valid. This field, not the unsigned X-Webhook-Test header, is what marks a rehearsal.

txid.description: The hash of the transaction the payment arrived with (empty until there is a payment).

type.description: Event kind: payment | payout | wallet | conversion — which body arrived.

on_error.description: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — stop processing after the first error.

payouts.description: An array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as in POST /v1/payout; order_id is required on each item and serves as the idempotency key: a retry returns the payout already created.

amount.description: The payout amount, as a string.

is_subtract.description: true — the fee is debited from the balance on top of the amount (the recipient gets exactly amount); false — from the payout amount.

network.description: Payout network; required if the asset lives on several networks.

amount.description: How much will be debited from YOUR balance, in currency (the fee included when you bear it); null — cannot be estimated right now (the fee is unknown and you bear it).

commission.description: The network fee of the payout, in currency; who bears it is fee_bearer. null — cannot be estimated right now (the fee oracle or the rate is unavailable), not zero: retry later.

fee_bearer.description: Who pays the network fee: gateway (Oblodai absorbs it, commission is 0), merchant (added to amount, the recipient gets the full sum) or recipient (deducted from payer_amount).

fee_type.description: exact — the fee is contractual (the gateway absorbs it); estimated — an oracle estimate.

network.description: The network — as it came in the request.

payer_amount.description: How much the RECIPIENT receives at the address, in currency (not what you pay — that is amount). null — cannot be estimated right now (the fee is unknown and the recipient bears it).

claimable.description: Can be claimed now: the link is funded and has not expired.

expires_at.description: Until when the link can be claimed (UTC).

passcode_required.description: Always true: amounts and network are shown after the passcode in the X-Claim-Passcode header.

status.description: Link state.

amount.description: The link amount — a promise to the recipient.

claimable.description: Can be claimed now: the link is funded and has not expired.

commission.description: Network fee; null — cannot be estimated right now (zero would mean the claim is free).

expires_at.description: Until when the link can be claimed (UTC).

fee_type.description: exact — the fee is fixed; estimated — an estimate based on the current network.

payer_amount.description: How much will reach the recipient; null — cannot be said (the fee was not estimated or ate the amount).

is_final.description: true — the status is final (confirmed / failed / cancelled).

is_refund.description: true — this is a payment refund, not a regular payout.

memo.description: The destination tag/memo passed at creation (TON Jetton, exchange memos). Empty — no memo.

refund_for.description: The id of the payment being refunded (null if this is not a refund).

Required on every link in a POST /v1/payout/link/batch: the batch's Idempotency-Key is not carried over to the items

address.description: Refund destination address. Defaults to the payment's payer_address; required only for Bitcoin/UTXO.

amount.description: The amount to refund, in the payment coin. Without it the refund is what is still refundable: the refundable amount less the refunds already made. The refundable amount is the most that all refunds of this payment together can send (refund.exceeds_refundable), and it follows the store's refund fee setting (getRefundFeeConfig). The payer's network surcharge is never refunded. When the customer bears the Oblodai commission, it is the amount paid minus the surcharge and the commission — what was credited to your balance for this payment. When you bear it, it is the amount paid minus the surcharge: the commission is paid from your balance, so the refunds debit more than the payment credited, and a balance too small for that fails with payout.insufficient_funds. POST /v1/payment/refund/calculate shows these numbers.

from_currency.description: Fund the refund by converting balance: USDT → the payment currency only. Needed when the payment coin has already been converted by auto-exchange.

order_id.description: Your order reference of the payment. Either uuid or order_id is required.

reference.description: An optional refund idempotency key: distinguishes two different refunds with the same (payment, address, amount); a retry with the same value returns the refund already made, also when amount is omitted. This is not order_id.

uuid.description: Payment id. Either uuid or order_id is required.

on_error.description: What to do when an item fails: continue (default) — process the rest; stop — stop processing after the first error.

refunds.description: An array of 1 to 5000 items — the same fields as in POST /v1/payment/refund; each item requires reference (the idempotency key) and the payment's uuid or order_id.

address_is_payer.description: true — address was omitted and the refund goes to the recorded payer_address (allowed only when payer_address_is_refundable = true); false — the address you passed.

amount.description: What this refund would send: the amount you passed, or by default the remaining refundable amount.

amount_paid.description: What the buyer paid in total, including the network surcharge.

commission.description: What is withheld from the refund besides the surcharge: with commission_bearer customer, the Oblodai commission as it was taken from each deposit (rounded up on each), plus the cost of collecting a swept deposit when there was one — together, what the payment did not credit you; 0 with merchant (you then pay the commission from your balance). amount_paid − surcharge − commission = refundable.

commission_bearer.description: Who bears the Oblodai commission on this refund — the store's refund fee setting (getRefundFeeConfig): customer — it is deducted from the refund, and the refunds return at most what the payment credited you; merchant — it is not deducted, and you pay it from your balance, so the refunds debit more than the payment credited.

credited.description: What this payment credited to your balance; null — cannot be reconstructed (a legacy payment).

currency.description: The refund coin — the one the buyer paid with.

from_amount.description: How much USDT the funding conversion would debit, at the current rate plus the conversion spread; it re-prices at execution. Present only with from_currency.

funded_by.description: The currency whose conversion would fund the refund (from_currency); present only then.

network.description: The network the refund would be sent on (canonical).

order_id.description: Your order_id of the payment; null if it has none.

rate.description: USDT per 1 unit of currency used for from_amount. Present only with from_currency.

refundable.description: The most that all refunds of this payment together may send; the surcharge is never refunded. commission_bearer customer: amount_paid minus surcharge minus commission, never more than credited. commission_bearer merchant: amount_paid minus surcharge (the surcharge counted per deposit), more than credited by the commission you pay from your balance.

refunded.description: Already refunded (live and completed refunds; failed and cancelled ones do not count).

remaining.description: refundable minus refunded: what can still be refunded before this refund.

surcharge.description: The payer's network surcharge inside amount_paid: the cost of accepting the deposit, never refunded from your balance. Counted per deposit, as the deposits were credited (rounded up on each), so amount_paid − surcharge − commission = refundable.

configured.description: true — the project set this setting itself; false — the gateway default applies.

fee_on_customer.description: The effective value for your refunds: the project setting, or the gateway default if there is none (automatic refunds then deduct the commission).

info.description:
Public HTTP API for accepting crypto payments and sending payouts and refunds. Every request is signed with your **API key** (`oblodai_…`), and the response comes in the envelope `{ "state": 0, "result": … }`.

## Quick start (in 3 steps)

1. Get an **API key** in the dashboard — **one key for everything**: accepting payments, payouts, refunds. It has a public id (`oblodai_…`) and a secret (`oblodai_live_…`, shown once).
2. Create an invoice: `POST /v1/payment` with the body `{"amount":"10","currency":"USD","order_id":"order-1"}`. The response contains a `url` — send the customer there, or show `address` + `payer_amount` yourself.
3. When the customer pays, we send you a **webhook** and the status becomes `paid`. That's it.

## Authentication (request signature)

Send three headers with every protected call:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-Public-Id` | the public id of your key (`oblodai_…`) |
| `X-Timestamp` | current Unix time in **seconds** |
| `X-Signature` | `hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<ts>\n<METHOD>\n<path>\n<Idempotency-Key>\n<body>"))` |

**The string to sign** is FIVE fields joined by `\n` newlines: the timestamp, the HTTP method, the path (with the query string, if any), the value of the `Idempotency-Key` header (**an empty string** if you do not send it) and the exact request body. The idempotency key is part of the signature because it is what decides whether a request is a retry or a new operation: if it were outside the signature, an intercepted request could be resent byte for byte with a different (or stripped) header to cause a second debit. A PHP example:

```php
$ts = time();
$idem = 'order-1';
$body = json_encode(['amount' => '10', 'currency' => 'USD', 'order_id' => 'order-1']);
$sign = hash_hmac('sha256', $ts."\n".'POST'."\n".'/v1/payment'."\n".$idem."\n".$body, $secret);
// headers: X-Public-Id: oblodai_…, X-Timestamp: $ts, X-Signature: $sign, Idempotency-Key: $idem
```

Requests outside the allowed clock-skew window are rejected — keep your clock in sync. **One key for everything:** this key authorizes accepting payments, payouts and refunds alike — guard its secret (if it leaks, you can reissue it in the dashboard).

## Response and error format

Success: `{ "state": 0, "result": { … } }`. Error: an HTTP 4xx/5xx code and the body `{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`. All money amounts are strings (so that no precision is lost).

## Idempotency (retries are safe)

Money calls are idempotent on a natural key — a retry never performs the action twice: payments and static wallets on `order_id` (a wallet — on `currency+network+order_id`), payouts on `order_id`, refunds on `(payment, address, amount)` with a cumulative "no more than was paid" cap. Incoming deposits are credited exactly once, no matter how many times the network rebroadcasts them (deduplicated on `(network, txid, output)`).

## Callbacks (webhooks)

When a payment's status changes we make a `POST` with a JSON body (the `Callback` shape: `type, uuid, order_id, amount, currency, payment_amount, payer_amount, payer_currency, status, is_final, txid, additional_data`) to your URL (`url_callback` of the payment/payout, or the project endpoint from `POST /v1/webhooks`). Delivery is **at least once** with retries for ~3 days (an endpoint that has not accepted a single attempt in 3 days is disabled automatically, and you get an email about it), so **your handler must be idempotent** (deduplicate on the body's `event_id`, see below). Verify the signature `X-Webhook-Signature: hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<unix>." + raw_body))`. Only the body is signed: decide nothing from any other delivery header — only the signature and its timestamp.

There are two different deduplication keys, and the difference matters: `X-Webhook-Id` identifies the DELIVERY (it is the same across retries of one delivery), while `event_id` in the body identifies the STATE. A resend via `POST /v1/payment/resend` is a new delivery of the current state: it has a new `X-Webhook-Id` and a HIGHER `sequence` (by design — a handler may discard a lower number as stale). The only thing they share is `event_id`, so that is what you must use to filter out what has already been processed. It is inside the signature; the same value also arrives in the `X-Webhook-Event-Id` header, which is not signed. A delivery from an older core may lack `event_id`; then deduplicate on `type`, `uuid`/`id` and `sequence` from the body. If after a reorg a payment becomes `paid` again with a different transaction, that is a different state and a different `event_id`, and such an event must be processed. A rehearsal (the test-webhook endpoints) carries `"test": true` in the body; that field, not the unsigned `X-Webhook-Test` header, is what marks it.

## Underpayment and overpayment, auto-refunds

The store sets an amount tolerance (`/v1/payment/accuracy/set`, 1–5% or disabled). Within the tolerance a payment is `paid`. Outside it: an **overpayment** (`paid_over`) auto-refunds the excess, and an expired **underpayment** (`wrong_amount`) auto-refunds the funds — both minus gas (and the fee, by default), to the payer's address (EVM/Tron/TON/Solana; Bitcoin/UTXO — manually). Toggled per store via `/v1/payment/autorefund/set` (both ON by default).

## Payment statuses

`select` (the customer is choosing a currency) · `created` (awaiting payment) · `confirm_check` (transaction seen, awaiting confirmations; a partial payment shows as `amount_remaining` > 0) · `paid` (paid) · `paid_over` (overpaid) · `wrong_amount` (underpaid, expired) · `expired` (expired) · `cancelled` (cancelled).

The `status` filter of `/v1/payment/history` accepts the same values — a status from a response or a webhook can be passed to the filter as is.

## Permission classes

Every operation signed with a merchant key carries the `x-oblodai-permission` extension: the permission class it needs. Your integration key has every class. A CLI key (issued by `oblodai login`) acts with the dashboard role of the team member who approved it, and each class needs a minimum role (the same table, machine-readable, is the spec's `x-oblodai-permissions` extension):

| Class | What it covers | Who may call it with a CLI key |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | What any team member sees in the dashboard: lists, cards, documents, reports, calculations | Viewer and above |
| `money` | What the dashboard lets a Finance member do without a per-operation second factor: invoices, static wallets, webhook registration, store settings, fee settings, approving payouts | Finance and above |
| `funds_out` | Operations that send the store's money out or decide where it goes: payouts, refunds, auto-withdrawal rules | never — the dashboard confirms each of these with 2FA, the store owner included, and a CLI key carries no per-operation factor; use the dashboard or the integration key |
| `settings` | Sandbox operations (a sandbox CLI key is issued to the store owner only) | Admin and above |
| `security` | What the dashboard reserves to the merchant owner — the API IP allowlist, keys, transfers to the owner's personal wallet — and every changing operation no dashboard screen offers (payment and payout links, batches, split rules, the checkout redirect, webhook secret rotation and on/off, test webhooks, payout cancellation and more) | never — integration key only |

A CLI key that may not call an operation gets `403 cli.permission_denied`; the error's `details` carry `required_role` (`viewer`, `finance`, `admin`, or `integration_key` for a `funds_out` or `security` operation), `role` (the key's role) and, for a `funds_out` operation, `reason: funds_out_dashboard_only`. The role follows the team: when it changes, the key acts with the new role from the next request, and a member removed from the team loses their CLI keys. An account loses all its CLI keys, in every store, after recovery, a password reset or change, "sign out of all other devices", a staff money freeze or suspension, and deletion; when a team owner deletes their account, the team's members lose their keys to its stores. Rotating the integration key with `revoke_previous` ("the key leaked") also revokes every CLI key of the store; a plain rotation leaves them alone. A CLI key lives 90 days; after that it is refused with `401 merchant.key_expired` — sign in again with `oblodai login`.

Where to send the buyer after payment (`success_url`) and after a failure (`fail_url`), and whether to email them a receipt (`email_receipts`).

The redirects are DEFAULTS: they apply only to invoices where you did not send `url_success`/`url_return` yourself. Values sent in `/v1/payment` always win. The receipt is not a default but a decision: the invoice has no field for it, and it is sent only if the buyer left an email.

Send only the fields you change: an omitted field keeps its previous value, and an empty string in a redirect means "do not redirect". The URL must be http(s); it is validated on write, not on display.

A public reference. It returns two lists, and they must not be confused:

- `currencies` — what you can **receive**: coins and their networks (plus flags for whether accepting and payouts are available).
- `pricing_currencies` — what you can **set a price in** (`currency` when creating a payment): the same coins **plus 45 fiat currencies** (`{"symbol":"EUR","decimals":2,"fiat":true}`) — USD, EUR, GBP, RUB, UAH, PLN, CZK, TRY, CNY, INR, BRL, CAD, AUD, CHF, AED, ZAR, MXN, IDR, THB, VND, NGN, JPY, KRW, SGD, HKD, NZD, SEK, NOK, DKK, ILS, SAR, PHP, MYR, TWD, PKR, LKR, MMK, BDT, ARS, GEL, HUF, BMD, BHD, KWD, CLP. The number of decimal places of each is in the `decimals` field (usually 2; JPY/KRW/VND/CLP — 0, BHD/KWD — 3) — take it from the response, do not hardcode it. Fiat has no networks and never will: you can price an invoice in it, but you cannot receive it.

The tenge, som and sum are not supported yet — the rate source does not quote crypto in them directly, and we will not derive a rate by multiplying two others.

post.summary: Choose the currency and network for a currency-agnostic link

post.description:
Creates an invoice and returns the address and amount to pay plus a link to the payment page.

**The simplest way:** pass `amount`, `currency` (the price currency, e.g. `USD`) and `order_id` (your order number). If you set `network` and `to_currency`, a specific coin/network is locked in immediately. If you DON'T, you get a currency-agnostic link: the customer picks the currency and network on the payment page.

**Price and settlement are different things.** `currency` says what the invoice COSTS: it can be fiat (`USD`, `EUR`, `RUB`, `GBP`, `JPY` and forty more fiat currencies — the full list is in `/v1/currencies`) or any coin. `to_currency` says what the customer PAYS WITH: **crypto only**. We do not hold fiat, so balances, payouts and refunds are always in a coin — you can issue an invoice for 5000 RUB, but it is paid in USDT, TRX, etc.

Hence the rule: if the price is in fiat, `to_currency` is either set explicitly or omitted together with `network` (then the buyer picks the coin). A fiat price with only `network` and no coin returns `payment.to_currency_required`: there is no way to derive a coin from rubles.

The yen and the won (`JPY`, `KRW`) have **no minor units** — write the amount without a fractional part (`"10000"`, not `"10000.00"`). The full list of price currencies is in `pricing_currencies` of `GET /v1/currencies`.

**Idempotency:** a retry with the same `order_id` returns the same invoice (no duplicate invoice is created).

Optional conveniences: `lifetime` (invoice lifetime in seconds, 300–43200), `url_return`/`url_success` (where to send the customer back), `url_callback` (where to send the webhook), `additional_data` (your private data), `payer_email`, `accuracy_payment_percent` (underpayment/overpayment tolerance, 0–5%), `is_refresh` (revive an expired invoice by order_id).

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` — the response was served from the one stored under the Idempotency-Key; the operation was not executed again.

post.description:
A refund is debited from your balance.

`address` (where to refund) may be omitted ONLY if the payment has `payer_address_is_refundable` = true: then we refund to the recorded payer address (`payer_address`). If it is false, we know the payer's address but it is not a refund address (Bitcoin/UTXO: the first input may belong to an exchange or be change; XRP: a shared exchange address with a destination tag; CARD payment via a crypto on-ramp: the sender is the provider's omnibus hot wallet, not the buyer). A refund sent there is irrecoverably lost to someone who never paid, so a request without `address` is rejected (`refund.no_address`): ask the buyer for an address and pass it explicitly. The payment's `uuid`/`order_id` is required. By default the remaining refundable amount is refunded; you may specify a partial `amount`. All refunds of a payment together cannot exceed its `refundable` amount (`refund.exceeds_refundable`), and the store's refund fee setting (POST /v1/payout/refund-fee-config/get) decides it. The payer's network surcharge is never refunded. When the customer bears our commission, `refundable` is what was paid minus the surcharge and the commission — what the payment credited to your balance. When you bear it, `refundable` is what was paid minus the surcharge: the commission is paid from your balance, so the refunds debit more than the payment credited, and a balance too small for that fails with `payout.insufficient_funds`. POST /v1/payment/refund/calculate shows these numbers without refunding.

Idempotent on `(payment, address, amount)`, and on `reference` when you pass it: a retry with the same `reference` returns the refund already made — also when `amount` is omitted, where the retry's own default would otherwise be the (now zero) remainder. Refunds to any address are approved automatically. The only exception is a card payment via an on-ramp: a refund TO THE RECORDED PAYER ADDRESS of such an invoice is rejected (`refund.omnibus_destination`), because that address belongs to the provider, not the buyer — send the buyer's address explicitly.

A refund is paid in THE SAME coin the buyer paid with. If it has already been converted into a stablecoin by auto-conversion, pass `from_currency: "USDT"` — the refund is funded by converting your USDT balance and remains a REFUND: the invoice is marked refunded and partner shares are reversed. You can also send the money as a regular payout, but reports will show it as a payout, not a refund.

x-mcp.description: Refund a received payment (by uuid or order_id) from your balance, in the coin the buyer paid with. Without amount it refunds what is still refundable, less earlier refunds. The payer's network surcharge is never refunded. The store's refund fee setting decides the rest: customer bears the commission — at most what the payment credited you; you bear it — paid minus surcharge, the commission coming from your balance. Pass address unless payer_address_is_refundable = true. Not for other transfers (payouts_create). Returns the refund payout. Side effect: sends money on-chain; irreversible.

post.description:
Takes the same body as POST /v1/payment/refund and answers what that refund would send — `amount`, `currency`, `network`, `address` (and whether it is the recorded payer's) — and the numbers behind it: `amount_paid`, the payer's network `surcharge` (never refunded from your balance), the `commission` withheld and who bears it (`commission_bearer`, the store's refund fee setting: with `merchant` nothing is withheld and you pay the commission from your balance), `credited`, the `refundable` ceiling for all refunds of the payment together, what is already `refunded` and what `remaining` can still go. With `from_currency` it also estimates the USDT the funding conversion would spend (`from_amount`).

Runs the same checks as the refund itself and fails with the same error the refund would (`refund.exceeds_refundable`, `refund.dust`, `refund.no_address`, `refund.nothing_to_refund`, …), including `payout.insufficient_funds` when your available balance does not cover the refund — which, when you bear the commission, can be more than the payment credited — and the payout controls the refund's payout meets: the payout freeze, your freeze, daily limit and per-payout limit, and whether the destination can receive this amount (`payout.destination_not_activated`). Not checked: the paid screening of the destination address, which runs when the refund is made; deposits that are not yet final, which the refund holds back (`payout.funds_maturing`); and, for a key that may not make refunds itself (a CLI key without the right to move money out), whether the address belongs to the gateway (`refund.destination_internal`) — the refund always checks it. Reserves and sends nothing; safe to retry.

post.description:
Refunds to `address` the NET amount received on a (blocked) static wallet: the amount already refunded is subtracted from what was received. While a refund is alive (created, sent, confirmed), a repeated call returns that same refund. If the refund did not go through (failed/cancelled), the call can be repeated — including to a different address. Deposits reverted by a reorg are not counted.

Blocking looks FORWARD: it stops the next incoming deposit, it does not revisit ones already credited. Money that arrives AFTER the block does not reach the balance — it goes to quarantine and waits for an operator's decision; you can refund it with this endpoint once the operator has reviewed it. Until then it is not yours yet, and the response will be "nothing to refund".

post.description: A disabled endpoint stops receiving deliveries: new events for this project are not queued, and those already queued are cancelled (status `cancelled`) and are not sent automatically after re-enabling. Needed when a receiver is decommissioned — otherwise every event would be retried for ~3 days and end up in the dead-letter queue indefinitely. The secret and URL are kept: enabling restores everything as it was. An endpoint for which not a single attempt has succeeded for 3 days in a row is disabled automatically — its queue is cancelled and the store owner gets an email; after fixing the receiver, enable it with this endpoint.

x-mcp.description: List recent webhook deliveries of your store, newest first: event type, status (pending, delivered, dead, cancelled), attempts, last error, URL. Use for "why did my webhook fail" or "why did it not arrive": last_error says what your endpoint answered. Do not use to send a test webhook (webhooks_send_test). post.description: Re-queues your delivery in status `dead` (retries exhausted) or `cancelled` (the endpoint was disabled): a fresh retry schedule, signed with the current secret. The delivery body is the same as in the log — to send the CURRENT state of a payment use `POST /v1/payment/resend`. Repeating the call is safe: a delivery already queued or delivered is returned as is with `ok: false`. Someone else's delivery — 404 `webhook.delivery_not_found`; a disabled endpoint — 409 `webhook.endpoint_disabled` (enable it first).

post.description:
Event `conversion.completed`. Sent when an economy-mode conversion is executed (completed — credited) or cancelled with the source amount returned (refunded).

Delivered to the project endpoint URL (POST /v1/webhooks) or to the object's `url_callback` if one was set at creation; always signed with the project endpoint's secret. Verification: the `X-Webhook-Signature` signature = hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, `<X-Webhook-Timestamp>` + "." + body)) over the body bytes as received, without re-encoding. Retries of one delivery carry the same `X-Webhook-Id`; a repeat of the same state (including a resend) carries the same `event_id` in the body — deduplicate on it (it is signed; the `X-Webhook-Event-Id` header carries the same value unsigned; a delivery from an older core may lack it — then use type:id:sequence from the body). Events of one object are ordered by `sequence` in the body: a lower number after a higher one is a late delivery. A body with `test: true` is a rehearsal and must be ignored. Headers are not signed: only the body and the signature headers decide anything.

2XX.description: Accepted: the delivery is closed, there will be no retries. The response body is not read.

default.description: Any other response — including 3xx (redirects are not followed) — no response within 10 s, or a dropped connection: the attempt fails and the delivery is retried with the same body, a fresh signature and the same X-Webhook-Id. Pauses before retries: 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min, 5 min, 10 min, 20 min, 30 min, 1 h, 1 h, 2 h, 2 h, 3 h, 3 h, 4 h, 4 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h, 6 h (each randomly extended by up to +20 %). 26 attempts in total over roughly 75 h; after the last one the delivery becomes dead and can be re-queued: POST /v1/webhooks/deliveries/requeue. An endpoint for which not a single attempt has succeeded for 3 d in a row is disabled automatically (re-enable: POST /v1/webhooks/active); deliveries to a disabled endpoint are cancelled.

request_vectors.name: get with query is signed over path+query

webhook.description: Only the body is signed: the signature covers "<ts>." + the raw body, and no other header is authenticated. Deduplicate on the signed body's `event_id` (named by event_id_field): it is the id of the object state, the same across retries and resends of that state, and always equal to the X-Webhook-Event-Id header (event_id_header), which is kept for compatibility but is not signed — prefer the body field. Current cores always send it; a delivery from an older core may lack it — then deduplicate on type:id:sequence from the signed body. Test deliveries (rehearsals) carry `"test": true` in the body; the X-Webhook-Test header (test_header) is not signed and marks nothing on its own.
